route_triple_comparison.description: out/ (local build) vs origin/gh-pages (deployed) vs live (curl) for 7 target routes

routes.note: Live serves root-level 857-byte alias (canonical→/heritage/, refresh→/services/) NOT the 3493-byte out/ file. gh-pages root file != out/ file.
Live serves gh-pages root file (canonical→/status/, refresh→/status/) not out/ file. out/ and docs/ both have /status-page/ canonical — deployed version differs.
Live serves gh-pages root file (canonical→/success-stories/) not out/ file (canonical→/use-cases/). out/ file is a real use-cases page; deployed version is an alias.
Live serves gh-pages root file (canonical→/services/, refresh→/services/) not out/ file. out/ has a real healthcare solutions page; deployed version is an alias.

out/ and docs/ have 3674-byte real page; gh-pages root has 864-byte alias (canonical→/services/, refresh→/services/). Live serves the alias. docs/ version (778 bytes) also differs from out/ (3674 bytes).
Live serves gh-pages root file (canonical→/book/) not out/ file (canonical→/free-consultation/). out/ has a real free-consultation page (3724 bytes); deployed version is a 1081-byte alias to /book/.
All three sources agree: canonical→self, no redirect. The 939-byte gh-pages file is a stub but serves correctly.

public_alias_directory.description: public/ serves as HTML alias layer (gh-pages ignores Netlify _redirects)
public_alias_directory.status_page_alias: public/status-page/index.html — canonical→/status-page/, meta-refresh→/status-page/ (self-referential, no external redirect)
public_alias_directory.financial_services_alias: public/industries/financial-services/index.html — canonical→self, full marketing page (NOT an alias)
public_alias_directory.notes: public/ aliases exist for status-page but NOT for industries/financial-services (which has a real marketing page in public/). This means the root-level industries/financial-services/index.html on gh-pages is a separate file, not served from public/.

redirects_comparison.root_redirects: local _redirects has /industries/financial-services and /free-consultation 200 rules pointing to index.html files
redirects_comparison.public_redirects: public/_redirects focuses on service/blog aliases; no /industries/financial-services or /free-consultation 200 rules
redirects_comparison.ghpages_redirects: origin/gh-pages:_redirects matches root _redirects (200 rules for target routes present)
redirects_comparison.live_redirects: Live _redirects does NOT contain /industries/financial-services or /free-consultation rules — GitHub Pages is NOT reading the Netlify-style _redirects file for these routes
redirects_comparison.conclusion: GitHub Pages serves the root-level index.html files directly. The _redirects file is not active on Pages for these routes. The deployed root-level files ARE the served content.

key_findings: FINDING 1 (root-level alias drift): gh-pages root level has 857-1081 byte alias files for 6 of 7 target routes. These files have canonical tags pointing to DIFFERENT URLs than out/ (e.g. /public-roadmap out/→self, gh-pages→/heritage/; /free-consultation out/→self, gh-pages→/book/). The live site serves these aliases, not the out/ files.

FINDING 2 (out/ files are the real pages): out/ contains full 3493-4749 byte pages for all 7 routes. These are the pages the local build produces. They are NOT deployed — the deployed versions are smaller alias/stub files.

FINDING 3 (docs/ vs out/ divergence for financial-services): docs/industries/financial-services/index.html is 3674 bytes (same as out/) but gh-pages docs/ version is 778 bytes. The docs/ tree on gh-pages has a stale/shorter version.

FINDING 4 (public/ alias layer incomplete): public/status-page/index.html exists as a self-referential alias (canonical→/status-page/, refresh→/status-page/). public/industries/financial-services/index.html is a full marketing page, not an alias. This explains why the root-level financial-services file on gh-pages is a separate file.

FINDING 5 (GitHub Pages _redirects ignored): Live _redirects does not contain /industries/financial-services or /free-consultation rules. GitHub Pages is serving root-level index.html files directly — the Netlify-style _redirects are not active on Pages for these routes.
FINDING 6 (tools/phishing-analyzer is the only consistent route): All three sources (out/, gh-pages, live) agree — canonical→self, no redirect, 200 OK. This is the only route without a mismatch.
FINDING 7 (BFS crawl clean): 94 pages crawled, 0 broken, 0 redirects. The site is internally consistent from a link perspective — no 404s or broken internal links.
discrepancy_description: The local build (out/) produces full pages for all 7 target routes. The deployed site (gh-pages root level) serves smaller alias/stub files for 6 of 7 routes, with canonical tags pointing to different URLs. The live site matches gh-pages, not out/. This is a content drift between local build and deployed site — the out/ files are not what is served.
recommended_action: Review whether the root-level alias files on gh-pages are intentional (they are lightweight 'not a packaged SKU' pages that redirect/canonical to real pages). If the out/ files are the intended content, the build/deploy process needs to copy out/ files to the root level of the Pages source, replacing the current alias files. If the alias files are intentional, reconcile the canonical tags so out/ matches what is deployed.
